Definition: properly, to breathe freely, i.e. revive; by implication, to have ample room
BiblicalUsage: Ravach is to breathe freely, to revive — to have ample room. When the evil spirit was upon Saul, David took a harp and played, 'so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him'; the king said, 'I will build me a wide house and large chambers'; and Elihu says, 'I will speak, that I may be refreshed.'
TheologicalSignificance: What I see here is that breathing freely is God's gift in distress: the music refreshed Saul, the wide house pleased the king, and Elihu spoke to breathe — and God gives room to breathe.
